title: Curated summary: Caring for skin wounds with or after cellulitis
text:
Caring for skin wounds during and after cellulitis. Curated summary of the CDC page "Preventing Group A Strep Infection". Group A strep is one of the most common causes of cellulitis.
Wound care (page section: "Wound care tips"):
Step 1: wash your hands with soap and water, or use an alcohol-based hand rub if washing isn't possible.
Step 2: clean all minor cuts and injuries that break the skin, like blisters and scrapes, with soap and water.
Step 3: after cleaning, cover draining or open wounds with clean, dry bandages. Change the bandages at least every few days until the wounds heal. Don't scratch or pick at the scab.
See a healthcare provider for punctures and other deep or serious wounds.
Protect wounds: if you have an open wound or skin infection, avoid hot tubs, swimming pools, and natural bodies of water such as lakes, rivers, and oceans. (Page section: "Protect wounds and infections".)
Antibiotics: take antibiotics as prescribed by your healthcare provider. (Page section: "Treat infections".)
Diabetes: if you have diabetes, check your feet daily for injuries or signs of infection. (Page section: "Limit exposure and spread of bacteria".)
curation_note: Team-written summary of the linked public page. Every number appears on that page; page sections are named in the text. Checked against snapshot cdc-group-a-strep-prevention.
